html:
Alfredo Stroessner was a Paraguayan general who ruled Paraguay as dictator from 1954 to 1989, one of the longest rules in modern Latin America.

A hero of the Chaco War, he took power in a coup in 1954 and ruled through the army and the Colorado Party. Elections were held but always won. Opponents were jailed, tortured or exiled, and the Aché people of the east were hunted and enslaved. His regime took part in Operation Condor with the other dictatorships of the region, as the Archives of Terror later showed.

He built roads and, with Brazil, the giant Itaipu Dam, and smuggling flourished in the city named after him, now Ciudad del Este. A coup by his own general removed him in 1989, and he died in exile in Brazil. Paraguay then began a slow move to democracy.
